chunks: Al-Husayn ibn 'Abdullah ibn Sa'id al-'Askari narrated to us. He said: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Ra'l al-'Abshami informed us. He said: Thubayt ibn Muhammad narrated to us. He said: Abu al-Ahwas al-Misri narrated to us. He said: A group from the people of knowledge narrated to us from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, peace be upon them. He said:

While the Commander of the Faithful, blessings of God be upon them, was in the most difficult stand at Siffin, a man from the tribe of Dudan stood up before him and said: What is the matter with your people that they pushed you away from this affair, while you are the noblest in lineage, the closest in connection to the Messenger, and the most knowledgeable of the Book and the Sunna?

He replied: You have asked, O brother of the Bani Dudan — and you have the right to ask and the bond of kinship — and indeed you are like one whose saddle-girth has loosened, releasing from a twisted rope. It is an authority over which the souls of some people were covetous, while the souls of others were generous in relinquishing it — and what an excellent Judge is God! So leave aside a plunder over which cries were raised in its enclosures, and come to the real matter regarding the son of Abu Sufyan, for time has made me laugh after making me weep. There is no wonder except in my neighbor and her question: 'Alas, do we have anyone?' I asked likewise. Wretched are the people who have lowered me! They have tried to practice deception in the religion of God.
If the trials of affliction are lifted from us, I shall carry them upon the pure essence of the truth. And if it be the other outcome, then 'do not grieve over the transgressing people' [5:26].
Away from me, O brother of Bani Dudan.

key_terms.أمير المؤمنين: Commander of the Faithful — a title of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib
key_terms.ابن أبي سفيان: the son of Abu Sufyan — Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan, the Umayyad governor who challenged Imam Ali's caliphate
key_terms.الأمر: the affair/authority — refers to the caliphate and political leadership of the Muslim community
key_terms.الإدهان: deception/sycophancy — attempts to corrupt or water down the religion through hypocrisy
key_terms.صفين: Siffin — the site of a major battle (37 AH/657 CE) between Imam Ali and Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about being denied the caliphate at the Battle of Siffin?
ai.summary: This hadith records a profound exchange at the Battle of Siffin (37 AH), where a man from Bani Dudan asks Imam Ali (AS) why Quraysh denied him the caliphate despite his superior lineage, closeness to the Prophet, and knowledge. Imam Ali responds with eloquent Arabic rhetoric, using proverbs and metaphors to explain that the caliphate was coveted by some and willingly relinquished by others, with God as the ultimate Judge. He then redirects attention to the immediate threat of Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan, quoting Quran 5:26 to express his resolve regardless of the outcome.

en.bilal-muhammad: Al-Husayn b. `Abdullah b. Sa`id al-`Askari narrated to us. He said: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim b. Ra`l al-`Abshami informed us. He said: Thubayt b. Muhammad narrated to us. He said: Abu’l Ahwas al-Misri narrated to us. He said: A group from the people of knowledge narrated to us from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad from his father from his grandfather (as). He said:

Amir al-Mu’minin (as) appeared at the most difficult stand in Siffin when a man from Bani Dudan went to him and said: What is the matter with your people who have pushed you away from this Order, even though you are the noblest in lineage, the closest to the Messenger, and the most knowing of the Quran and the Sunna?

So, he said: You have asked – O brother from Bani Dudan, and you have the right to ask, and the right of kinship – and you are anxious and distressed, and you ask of something unintentionally. This is a time that has deprived the souls of one people and spoiled the souls of the other – and Allah is the best of judges. So, abandon the story of loss, which has left hues and cries in its place, and tend to the speeches of the son of Abi Sufyan, for time has made me laugh after it has made me weep. There is no wonder except in my neighbour and her question; alas, do we have anyone to ask this to the people that have lowered me? They have tried to slander the religion of Allah.
If the trials and afflictions were lifted from us, I would carry them to the very core of the truth. But, if it happens to be otherwise, “then do not grieve over the transgressing people.” [5:26]
To you, from me, O brother from Bani Dudan.
